questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Even though my main purpose of going on exchange was to get to explore a new culture and to gain new perspectives, it was also important for me, that my university of choice offered interesting and relevant courses, that would fit with the rest of my education. Due to Covid-19, it was also important to me, that the university was in Europe. It was also crucial to me, that the courses at the destination were offered in English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was pretty easy to find most information needed upon arrival. We had a really great coordinator at the Department of Sociology at the University of Vienna, who was always ready to answer questions quickly. The process of choosing and applying for the different courses could have been easier and better explained, as that was a bit stressful. Also, the process of applying for an address in Austria could have been a bit better supported. However, in my experience, everything worked out fine and overall there was always information to be found, and people to ask for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were offered an online meeting before arrival, with practical information, which was really great, as it fixed some concerns and we also got to talk to some of the other exchange students. I was also offered to be teamed up with a local student upon arrival. Furthermore, we had a coordinator at the specific department at the University of Vienna, who helped with a lot of the practical stuff, especially in the beginning. I was lucky to live with local flatmates, who could also help me with most of my questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was really lucky, and found housing quickly by applying to a post in a Facebook Group. There are several different FB groups about housing in Vienna. Many of my friends also lived in dorms - a recommendation here is to apply as early as possible. A few of the people I met there struggled a lot with finding housing, and one even had to stay in a hostel for the first month. In my experience though, it is almost always possible to find somewhere, and the University can also help with finding dorms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Vienna almost every housing is "off campus". Vienna is such a great city, and I would recommend people to find the housing that fits them best. I've heard good experiences about both WG's (shared flats), dorms and one person apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration itself was pretty easy and explained along the way. The process of choosing courses however, was confusing and stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information on the website, and I was also e-mailed a lot of information along the way. There was also help to be found by asking the coordinators both at my home university and Uni Wien.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful, and got most of the ones I wanted - I think that differs a lot though, depending on the department. It was also difficult to get exactly 30 ECTS, as Uni Wien generally offers less points per course, compared to my home university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions offered along the way, and don't panic about the course selection. If you want to follow a course from another department than your own, it's best to know a bit earlier, as you need a signature from the specific apartment, and not just your own coordinator.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was a BA student, but I was also allowed to do MA courses at my stay. Furthermore, I did a German language course, which is linked to Uni Wien, but not specifically BA or MA level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were lectures, so they were very similar to the ones at UCPH. There was less group work, but that is solely due to the courses I chose, and not the University itself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sustainable Solutions for Planetary Health (2 ECTS). German Course (8 ECTS). Introduction to Cultural Theories (5 ECTS). Climate Change and Climate Crisis - Transformative Concepts and Innovations Gruppemerit (5 ECTS). Approaching Cultural Studies (5 ECTS). Culture, Society and the Media (5 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend a language course, if you're interested in German (you can also do less than 8 ECTS, or do it before the semester start). It's a different type of learning, and links you to the country you're on exchange in.

The course "Culture, Society and the Media" was really interesting. It's about representations of nature and nonhuman bodies in media and culture, and offers a lot of alternative perspectives and ways of thinking about the world we live in, than any course I've ever had.

"Climate Change and Climate Crisis" was really interesting, as it was a collaboration between the university and Fridays for Future. Every time, there was a new speaker, specialized in their own field, guesting and teaching the lectures. This was a new and inspiring way to do a course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a student ticket for the public transportation in Wien - however it's much more expensive, if you only set your Vienna address as "secondary". Furthermore, I struggled a lot to access the ticket in the beginning, and eventually just bought a regular one, as it was easier. I ended up using way more than expected on transportation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is generally less expensive in Wien than in CPH. Most groceries, food and drinks are also less expensive in Wien, but not by a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports offered by the Uni, but it was difficult to sign up for them, and they were booked quickly. The ESN programme connected with the UNI however, was really great and offered some nice events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different sports, debate club, choir etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend researching the stuff offered, but I would also recommend searching for stuff outside uni. I ended up joining a local fitness boxing club (Backyard Vienna), and I was also in a WhatsApp Chat about bouldering, where it was easy to just meet up with others at the different climbing gyms.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is A LOT to do in Wien, but it's also easy to travel to other parts of Austria by train or bus. There is a lot of beautiful nature, even just on the border of Vienna. It's also easy and quick to get to e.g. Bratislava, Budapest or Prague for getaways.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy in my experience, but I was also lucky to share a flat with two locals, so I was introduced to many of their Austrian friends. For me, that was the perfect combination - living with locals and getting to know their network, and on the other hand meeting a lot of international students through the Erasmus Network.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Practice German. Join social events or a sports club. Choose courses with group projects.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The waiters of Vienna are known to be a bit rude - which in some cases is true. You just need to learn not to take it personally. Furthermore, Austrian humor is often sarcastic and dark, and locals will respect you more when you can also make fun of yourself, and not be offended by them joking with you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of very strong traditions, and they use a lot of energy and ressources, going out of their way to make a big deal out of Christmas decorations and ice skating arenas fx. That is pretty cool. All the Austrians I've met are very welcoming and including, and ready to help with whatever, if you ask for it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to fill out the "Meldezettel" upon arrival in Austria, stating that you moved there.
Take part in the WhatsApp groups provided in the beginning - then it's really easy to meet other exchange students.
Use your mobility coordinator - they are there to help you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It's nice to know, that you can do a language course before the semester, if you want to.
The exams are quite different than in DK - most of them are very short, and you don't get to apply your knowledge as much. In my experience, they were more about "repeating" what we had learned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Wien is such a nice, beautiful and great city. I felt very "at home" there, almost from the beginning, and most of my friends felt the same way. The social exchange and meeting so many great people (both locals and other international students) was very rewarding. It was also great to be able to try out some other courses, than those offered at UCPH, and also just actually completing a whole semester in a foreign country and to pass the exams is a big victory.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was a lockdown and some of the courses were online due to Covid, which was a bit of a challenge. The exam period was also intense, as it was different than at UCPH, and all the courses are taught until the date of the exam.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Wien is a perfect place to live, I'm sure you will love it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
